newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Transaero plans Moscow-Chicago service in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Transaero plans Moscow-Chicago service in 1997.

text.p: Russia's leading private airline, Transaero, plans to launch regular passenger flights between Moscow and Chicago in 1997, a company official said on Wednesday.
President Alexander Pleshakov told Reuters that Transaero would use Chicago as a base from which to develop other routes in the United States.
He also said Transaero and its rival, state-owned Aeroflot, had begun a cooperation programme.
"We agreed that Transaero will develop its Moscow-Los Angeles service while Aeroflot will expand its routes to Seattle and San Fransisco," he said.
An aviation source in Moscow said Aeroflot planned to give Transaero its Moscow-Los Angeles route.
Pleshakov also said Transaero would improve its cargo operations.
"We had a good load factor in 1995 and plan to increase cargo deliveries this year, operating three leased DC-10 jets," he said, adding that the carrier did not plan to buy or lease freighters.
Transaero hauled 3,700 tonnes of cargo in the first eight months of this year, compared to 1,340 tonnes in the same period of 1995.
Pleshakov said Transaero might change its tarrifs on international routes for its winter schedule, but gave no details.
AO Transaero was established in 1991 and flies to 21 destinations in the former Soviet Union and seven other international destinations.
The airline has launched six new international and domestic regular routes this year.
